description: GDPR requires opt-in (default deny); CCPA permits opt-out (default allow). The target fan.consent_preference carries a boolean, which cannot express the difference between "not asked" and "declined".

The identity observed, not the resolved profile. Nullable because an event can arrive for an identity the graph has not yet seen. Resolving events to profiles at write time would rewrite history every time the identity graph changed.
The extraction watermark. Mobile SDKs buffer offline and backfill, so event timestamp is not monotonic -- an extract keyed on timestamp loses late events permanently.
Whether the namespace asserts a human rather than a browser or device. Stitching on a non-person identity is how a shared household device merges two fans into one profile.

Why a message was not sent. A consent_denied suppression is a compliance record demonstrating the opt-out was honoured -- materially different from a delivery failure, and target fan.communication merges the two.

The sparse remainder of the XDM record. JSONB rather than columns because the schema is customer-defined and most fields are null for most profiles -- flattening would produce a table of mostly nulls.
Which merge policy produced this view. The same identities under two policies yield two different profiles; target fan.fan_profile records one.
The segment rule verbatim. Target fan.segment stores a name and a description, so what the segment actually means is not recoverable downstream.
`realized` is newly qualified, `existing` is continuing, `exiting` has just dropped out. The exit is the actionable state and the target model's membership boolean cannot express it.
NUMERIC(9,6) -- roughly 0.1 m resolution. model.json declares DECIMAL(9,6) and the generated target DDL emits DECIMAL(18,2), losing four digits.
The upstream model flags its equivalent column ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE with seven stripped values. Restored here as a CHECK: single-table use.
Business key into tm_axs.event.event_code. Not a foreign key -- different database. The pair is resolved through common.entity_xref.
Gate count, which is what the target fixture.actual_attendance receives. Differs from seats_sold by no-shows, and the gap is the point.
Stated capacity, not a count of manifest_section rows. It is signed off by the fire authority and is the figure reported to the league.
Retained alongside prior_seat_count so partial churn is visible. An account dropping from six seats to two is a renewal in the target model.
Explicit sort order. Row labels are alphanumeric and inconsistent, so distance from the field is not derivable from the label.
Relocation and renewal priority. Derived from tenure, spend and account standing by rules that live in the application, not here.
Marks the record that wins survivorship for this canonical_id, i.e. the system whose attribute values are kept when two sources disagree.
Materialised path, kept alongside parent_folder_id. Asset trees are deep and read constantly but rearranged rarely, so the redundancy pays.
A media object with no essence. Normal and intended: the production order reserves the object before the camera has shot anything.
Frames, not seconds. Broadcast operations are frame-accurate and a rounding to seconds loses the edit point. Target content.asset carries a duration in seconds.
Nullable, and the null is meaningful: a live publication with no rights window behind it is either wholly owned content or an unlicensed publication, and only the first is acceptable.
Inbound rights are bought, outbound are sold. One table holds both, and an extract that ignores direction counts acquired rights as revenue.

The classic local-blackout term: no local broadcast until the venue sells out. It couples a rights rule to live ticketing inventory, which is the single clearest cross-system dependency in the whole model.
As-run duration. A match going to extra time shifts every subsequent item, and the scheduled-versus-actual gap is what the target broadcast.broadcast_schedule cannot show.
Human or machine, and which kind of machine. Target content.asset_tag does not distinguish, so an unverified AI guess and a librarian's judgement arrive in the lakehouse indistinguishable.
An open vocabulary lets operators add terms as they tag. Useful, and the reason controlled vocabularies drift -- which is what the target content.metadata_tag inherits.

Derived from the video offset at write time and then frozen. If the offset is later corrected, already-published instances keep the minute they were reported with, which is what downstream consumers cited.
Normalised 0..100 rather than metres, so positions are comparable across venues with different pitch dimensions. Target event.scoring_event has no spatial columns at all.
Exclusive groups allow one label per instance, inclusive groups several. The distinction is what makes a label set queryable rather than a bag of tags, and the target model has no equivalent.
UUID, generated client-side. Analysts code matches offline and sync later, so identifiers cannot depend on server coordination.
The coding pass this figure was computed from. Target athlete.performance_stat drops it, so a disputed statistic cannot be traced back to the instances behind it.

Milliseconds of video before the match begins. Instances are timed in video milliseconds, so this offset is what converts an instance position into a match minute. Without it the target scoring_event minute is wrong.
Reversal document. Posted documents are never updated or deleted, so corrections appear as a second document -- and a naive extract that sums without excluding reversals double-counts.
Reference key into the originating system. For ticketing revenue this carries the TM/AXS billing document, which is what makes the order-to-ledger reconciliation possible at all.

column_default:
CASE
    WHEN (shkzg = 'S'::bpchar) THEN dmbtr
    ELSE (- dmbtr)
END
description: Generated from SHKZG and DMBTR. SAP stores amounts unsigned with the debit/credit sign in a separate character; extracts that miss this produce a trial balance that does not net to zero.

Cost centre code only. Deliberately unconstrained: CSKS is time-dependent and keyed on a validity date this row does not carry, so resolution means picking the CSKS row whose DATAB..DATBI window contains BUDAT.
Profit centre code only. Unconstrained for the same reason as KOSTL: CEPC is time-dependent. Joining on code alone fans out across every version.
Not a real SAP field. Four target tables -- league.conference, league.division, league.team and finance.profit_center -- all map to this one table, and this column is what tells them apart.
Valid-to date, and part of the primary key -- SAP keys time-dependent master data this way. The target finance.cost_center keeps one row per cost centre, so the extract must pick the window in force.
SAP deletion flag. Rows are marked, not removed -- so an extract that ignores it will load prices that are no longer in force.
Unrestricted-use stock. Deliberately not CHECKed non-negative: SAP permits negative stock in some configurations, and a constraint here would reject rows a real extract delivers.
Client. Leading key column of every table in this schema. A production system also holds test and training clients, so an extract that does not filter on MANDT returns duplicate business rows.
Not a real SAP field. Added so the league/franchise/operating-company distinction is explicit rather than inferred from naming, since this table is doing double duty as the league structure.
Accounting release status: A not released, B partial, C released, E error. Only C has hit the ledger, so revenue reporting that ignores this column counts invoices that do not yet exist in the GL.

Not a real SAP field. Eight target tables map to this one table, and without an explicit category the extract would have to infer the contract type from the account group or the document type -- which is how wrong rows end up in athlete.contract.
The earlier employment of the same person. A player returning as a coach is one person with two employments, and this link is what keeps the career continuous.
Why this effective-dated row exists. Distinguishes a promotion from a transfer from a loan return; target athlete.roster keeps none of it, so the reason for every squad change is lost downstream.

Pick number, for a draft-type requisition. The closest a recruiting module gets to a draft -- it cannot represent traded picks or compensatory selections, which is why target athlete.draft_selection is mapped at low confidence.
Governs work eligibility and, in most competitions, squad registration limits on non-domestic players. A competition-rules field as much as an HR one.
A vacant position is the unit of workforce planning: "fourteen stewards needed for this fixture" is a statement about positions, not people. Target venue.staff_plan is built from these.
Recycle Bin flag. Records remain queryable for 15 days after deletion; an extract that does not filter this loads records the business considers gone.
The replication watermark. Moves on platform-driven changes that leave last_modified_date untouched, so an extract keyed on last_modified_date silently misses rows.
Business key into adobe_aep.journey. Salesforce plans the campaign; AEP executes it. Target fan.communication comes from the AEP side.

column_default:
CASE
    WHEN ((first_name IS NULL) OR ((first_name)::text = ''::text)) THEN (last_name)::text
    ELSE (((first_name)::text || ' '::text) || (last_name)::text)
END

description: Inferred from third-party marketing data, not declared by the fan. Worth treating more carefully than declared attributes, not less.
Why a deal was lost. No target column corresponds, so the lakehouse can report what was won but not why anything was lost.

column_default:
CASE
    WHEN ((list_price IS NULL) OR (list_price = (0)::numeric)) THEN NULL::numeric
    ELSE (((list_price - unit_price) / list_price) * (100)::numeric)
END

description: VARCHAR(121) -- Salesforce computes Name as FirstName + space + LastName at 40 and 80 characters respectively. The odd width is the platform's, not a typo.
Polymorphic reference -- may point at an Opportunity, Contract, Campaign or Case. Cannot be a foreign key, which is why what_object_type is mandatory alongside it.
A smart collection has no membership rows -- it is a stored rule. Target merchandise.product_category therefore cannot be fully populated from collection_product alone.
The `redacted` state is a completed GDPR erasure. It is not the same as unsubscribed and must not be loaded as a marketable state.
The money this discount actually cost on this line. The only place promotion effectiveness can be measured; neither target merchandise.promotion nor order_line retains it.
Deliberately permits negative values: a variant with inventory_policy `continue` oversells by design, and a non-negative CHECK would reject rows a real extract delivers.

Line-level personalisation -- shirt name and number for sports kit. JSONB because the keys are retailer-defined. Target merchandise.order_line has no equivalent, so customisation is lost and with it the reason the item cannot be resold.
Negative by Shopify convention -- a 20%% discount is -20. The CHECK is there because sign inversion on load is a real and silent failure.
`continue` permits overselling. Target merchandise.sku_catalog has no equivalent, so the lakehouse cannot distinguish a genuine stockout from a deliberate backorder.
Sizing accounts for most apparel returns, and separating too-small from too-large is what makes the data actionable on the size curve. Target merchandise.return_request has a single reason column.
Nullable: guest checkout is normal. Target merchandise.merch_order expects a fan reference, so guest orders need a synthetic identity or they fall out of fan-level revenue reporting.
Denormalized deliberately. The address as shipped must not change when the customer edits their address book afterwards.
Native array. A Plus shop presents prices in several currencies; the target model has one currency column, so conversion happens on load.
Test-mode transactions are real rows with no money behind them. An extract that does not exclude them inflates revenue.
Opaque handle to a template held in the access-control appliance. Biometric data itself is deliberately not stored in this tier.
Self-reference to the surviving account. The upstream model tags 22 columns self_ref_fk; duplicate-merge chains are the commonest case.
Health-adjacent free text (pii_health in the upstream tagging). Should not propagate to the lakehouse without an explicit lawful basis.
Local calendar date at the venue. Retained separately from scheduled_start_at because the UTC instant alone does not determine it.
Business key into archtics.event_manifest. Resolved through common.entity_xref on entity_type = fixture. Not a foreign key.
Generated column. The target model stores a single ticket price; this is the figure it receives, with the component split retained here.
Business key into sap_s4.vbrk. Null until revenue posts, which is the ticketing-to-finance reconciliation gap.
Native INET. The target model types its equivalent as STRING; the upstream tagging marks it pii_ip.
Reader buffered the scan while offline. Such rows arrive late and out of order, which is why the ingestion watermark uses uploaded_at, not scanned_at.
Business key into archtics.building. Not a foreign key -- different database. Resolved through common.entity_xref on entity_type = 'venue'.
Revenue is stored negative in many Adaptive models. Loading a flipped account without reversing the sign inverts the whole P&L, and nothing in target finance.budget records that the flip was needed.
A balance account carries its closing value forward; a flow account sums across periods. Summing a balance account across twelve months is a classic and silent twelvefold overstatement.
NUMERIC(20,6) because a cell holds currency amounts and driver rates alike -- headcount, occupancy percentage, price per seat. Rounding drivers to two places breaks the calculation they feed.
A calculated cell is formula output, not a plan. Loading it into target finance.budget as a planned figure double counts against its inputs.
A dimension member is usually a business entity from another system -- a fixture, a player, a sponsor. This is the business key, and it is how a planning cell resolves to anything real.
A rollup level holds no input of its own, only the sum of its children. An extract that loads rollup levels alongside leaves double counts.
The planning calendar, which need not match the SAP fiscal year variant. When they differ, budget-versus-actual comparison requires a period remap that target finance.budget does not record.
